english.title: Supply / install gaming machine not in accordance with operating licence / exception - Gambling Act 2005

english.legislation: Contrary to sections 243(1) and 246(1) of the Gambling Act 2005.

english.notes:
(i) Section 243(1)(b) of the Gambling Act 2005 provides exceptions to the offence if the person makes the gaming machine available for use by an individual, and the individual does not, by using the machine, acquire an opportunity to win a prize, section 248 of the Gambling Act 2005, and if the person supplies or installs the gaming machine in accordance with a single-machine supply and maintenance permit under section 250 of the Gambling Act 2005.
(ii) Section 243(3) of the Gambling Act 2005 exempts from this offence the supply of a gaming machine/part of a gaming machine as scrap (without any element of salvage), or incidental to the sale or letting of property on which the machine has previously been used in reliance on a provision of the Gambling Act 2005.
(iii) For the territorial application of this section see section 251 of the Gambling Act 2005.

other.penalty:
Fifty one weeks imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
12 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
